> Jane — thanks for the quick flag. I'm escalating internally and opening a war room.
> 
> Immediate asks:
> - Dylan / Monica: can you validate whether this correlates with yesterday's proxy multiplexing rollout?

Quick update after an initial triage of the traces:
- Reproduced locally with a stress harness: when multiple concurrent streams are multiplexed onto a single TCP connection and a proxy-level frame coalescer is enabled, header boundaries can be split across kernel recv() calls. Our SDK's streaming parser assumes header lines arrive atomically and uses a lightweight line-oriented state machine. If the first header fragment arrives alone and the remainder follows in the next read, the parser mis-classifies the frame boundary and drops the header block — the application sees a half-open stream and eventually times out.
- This is most likely a client-side parsing resilience issue compounded by the new proxy coalescing behavior; server returns are fine.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Hotfix the SDK streaming parser to tolerate fragmented header frames (small change to accumulate until double-CRLF).
2) Provide a configuration knob to disable request multiplexing at the client for BrightSide as an immediate workaround.
3) Create an automated test in the integration harness to simulate recv() fragmenting.

I've attached repro steps and a minimal harness (repro-instruction-steps.md). Will follow up with a failing unit demonstrating the split-header case.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

- Impact: elevated latency, increased 5xx failures, important checkout flows affected for BrightSide during peak.
- Severity: P1 for the customer; potential SLA credit exposure if not mitigated within next 8 hours.

Immediate plan:

B) Ops will coordinate a targeted traffic shift to the legacy connector for BrightSide as stop-gap (Dylan, can you coordinate with their infra?).

Dylan — please confirm you can perform the traffic reroute and provide timing. I'll open JIRA INS-4729 and tag the SDK hotfix.
